Five numbers from 50 to 99 every gladiator carries: [[spd|Speed]], [[str|Strength]], [[int|Intelligence]], [[lck|Luck]] and [[cha|Charisma]]. Crossing 76 (and higher bands) earns a perk. Perks pay only in rounds that allow class abilities, and they stack.
Movement. Base 3 (two legs); +1 at 76, +2 at 96. Grows with drills and fights.
Damage per successful attack: +1 at 76, +2 at 87, +3 at 96. Grows with drills, wins and kills.
How a CPU plays the gladiator: Easy below 76, Normal from 76, Hard from 96. Grows by surviving and winning.
Coin each turn: +1 at 76, +2 at 96. Grows with time at a ludus and the bonds you build.
Crowd Favor each turn: +1 at 76, +2 at 96. Grows with big crowds, high CF, fame and being spared.
Every gladiator has five ratings from 50 to 99. Classes set the loadout; the ratings set the perks. A Slave tends to be fast and a Soldier strong, but not every one is.
Speed: +1 movement at 76, +2 at 96. Strength: +1 damage per hit at 76, +2 at 87, +3 at 96. Luck: +1 coin a turn at 76, +2 at 96. Charisma: +1 CF a turn at 76, +2 at 96. They stack.
When they pay: only in rounds that allow class abilities. In a Classic event that is round 1, so a strong gladiator should hit early and hard.
Intelligence sets a CPU's mind — Novice below 65, Apprentice 65, Fighter 76, Veteran 86, Master 96. It never adds gear or coin.
Slow and steady: a busy, winning fighter climbs about one band a season. Gains slow above 90 and stop at 99.

What grows what: Strength and Speed from the Training Yard (brutal drills most), fights survived and won, and kills. Intelligence from surviving and winning. Charisma from big CF, fame and being spared. Luck from weeks with your house and the bonds you build (meals, bonuses, kin tickets).
Watch the free agents: they drill on their own, and rival yards train too. A fighter who reaches 96 makes the news.
Your mail carries a weekly growth report from the doctores; a new band also makes your ludus ledger.

This is a digital standalone edition of D.Soto's board game Flavius Rule — built from the original Magnus Edition on Tabletop Simulator and the Print & Play Edition sold through Barnes & Noble.

Behold! I implore you all to embark on any daring quests of creativity one can devise, embracing even the most obscure ideas, for the wisdom gained on these paths shall surpass any mere creation. In the year 2016, I set forth on a momentous journey that has forged the very essence of Flavius Rule as you now behold it. From humble beginnings, tiny sparks of inspiration ignited, propelling me into uncharted territories where new, exhilarating challenges awaited. As I now reach the culmination of this odyssey, should this game kindle even a flicker of entertainment, joy, or inspiration within a select few, I shall consider my mission triumphantly fulfilled, surpassing all initial aspirations.

I extend profound gratitude to my esteemed Flavius community, the valiant fr-qa-team, the venerable Indie Game Lab, and the illustrious board game design communities for their invaluable contributions, their sagacious counsel, and the endless wellspring of provided inspiration. Furthermore, I humbly express boundless love and reverence to my father, who lent his guiding hand in designing and constructing the very first prototype of Flavius Rule, forever etching his legacy into this immersive realm.

Finally, I pour my heartfelt appreciation to each and every one of you, noble players, for it is through your participation that the spirit of Flavius Rule is brought to life. May your ventures within this ancient realm resonate with valor, cunning, and a glimmer of the divine. God bless & Bonam fortunam!
